state.case_summary:
A 76-year-old woman presented with one week of right hip pain and difficulty walking. She had received denosumab for osteoporosis for five years and had undergone total hip arthroplasty for a left femoral neck fracture two years earlier. On examination, her Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) score was 96 on the right and 76 on the left. Initial plain radiographs at an outside clinic were reportedly normal. Repeat radiographs at our hospital demonstrated an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck. Computed tomography confirmed a lateral cortical fracture without comminution, and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a high-signal bend in the same region. Bone mineral density was 0.840 g/cm2 in the lumbar spine and 0.899 g/cm2 in the right femoral neck. Laboratory studies revealed calcium 9.7 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 47 IU/L, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase-5b 104 mU/dL, type I procollagen N-terminal propeptide 21.9 μg/L, and osteocalcin 4.9 ng/mL.
